About

About Nolan Kido

The person, not just the topics

I'm Nolan Kido. My work brings together practical AI, business operations, and accounting research. I build and examine tools for real tasks, then show the checks and limits behind them. AI Works Human Decides is the principle connecting it all.

A few things you can verify

There are different kinds of evidence behind my work. A research publication shows a contribution to accounting scholarship. A project record shows what a particular tool does and what was checked. My poker record and videos show another part of my life. None of these is a substitute for judging the work itself.

Research / Peer-reviewed publication

Published accounting research

I coauthored The Influence of Elections on the Accounting Choices of Governmental Entities, published in the Journal of Accounting Research in 2012. The MIT repository has the author's manuscript.

Practical AI / Working example

A local-AI project and its checks

Review Reply Writer drafts customer replies with a local model. The public case explains the workflow, while a separate evidence audit tests archived fictional examples and deliberately altered controls.

Poker / Public record and videos

Tournament poker with Nolan

I play tournaments and publish first-person stories. My player page links independent results where available and distinguishes reported finishes from my own NolanPoker videos.

The research concerns governmental accounting, not AI performance. The AI examples are bounded demonstrations, not audited business outcomes. Tournament cashes are gross results, not profit.

How I handle credibility claims: Inspect the before-and-after audit of this website's public identity data. It shows which professional claims were removed pending better evidence, which authored work stayed linked, and why correcting metadata is not proof of higher search rankings.

AI is part of how I build, write, and explore ideas. What interests me is not just what a tool can produce, but whether the result helps with something that matters. I want technology to make more room for life, not give every part of it another dashboard.

That is the connection between the different parts of this site. Practical technology, thoughtful living, tournament poker, and creative work ask different questions, but all involve attention, judgment, and the willingness to learn.

What matters to me in the work

Usefulness: start with a real purpose, not a demonstration in search of one. Clarity: give the reader enough context to understand the choice. Judgment: be willing to question a polished result, change direction, or stop when the work has done its job.

Those are priorities, not a claim that every attempt succeeds. Let AI do more. Keep the judgment. develops the distinction behind them.

What I spend my attention on

Technology is where I explore useful AI and software: starting with an actual need, checking what comes back, and knowing what still needs a person's judgment.

Living Well leaves space for meaning, spirituality, relationships, and the texture of ordinary life. Some questions deserve exploration rather than an efficient answer. Its free resource library offers ways to follow those questions.

Tournament poker combines play, uncertainty, and study. The poker section makes room for understanding the game and reviewing decisions, without confusing a good result with a good decision. My tournament player profile links to independently recorded event results.

Writing and visual storytelling are another way of working through an idea. I care about what the reader or viewer can understand and feel, not just what a tool makes possible.

Outside the categories

Food, travel, and the experience of learning something unfamiliar belong in the picture too. Not every interest needs to become a project or a public update.

I keep this site focused on the ideas and material that are useful to share. Some work and much of ordinary life belong outside a public website.

Practical AI projects and creative work

  • Review Reply Writer uses local AI to draft customer replies, with the owner's policy and saved-text approval kept in the workflow.
  • Preflight checks book-series continuity against source passages. Its case includes useful findings, incorrect flags, and missed details.
  • Dinner on Time is a cooking-planner simulation developed with AI assistance. Its recorded demonstration shows a schedule changing after an oven delay.
  • Poker comics connect another interest with visual storytelling, pairing AI-generated artwork with readable explanations and rules notes.

Methods behind the projects: My local AI gaming-laptop guide records setup, privacy boundaries, and test limitations. A separate review-reply evidence audit checks archived fictional examples and deliberately altered controls. Neither record establishes measured business impact, and the laptop guide does not report a laptop-speed benchmark.

Three things you can inspect directly

The best introduction is a small set of public examples rather than an impressive-sounding list of claims. These three starting points do different jobs: one is a tool, one is a recorded release, and one explains the judgment behind the work.

The practical method: AI Works Human Decides means choosing the right task, bounding AI's role, checking the result independently, and leaving the final call with a person. The examples below let you inspect parts of that process. They do not establish a universal success rate.

Use a tool: The AI task brief builder turns your own inputs into a structured brief with checks and boundaries. There is no AI call. You can inspect how it works and what it cannot do. It is not a measured productivity result.

Inspect a recorded case: Follow an AI-assisted website repair, including the defect, the separate checks and their limits. For a smaller instructional contrast, try an independent-checking example. The recorded release is evidence about one defect, not a claim that every AI-assisted change is safe.

Understand the approach: Let AI do more. Keep the judgment. makes the case for retaining purpose and responsibility. Ask whether a tool actually helps, or use the full time-cost calculator to model the work it adds as well as the time it may remove. An essay is a perspective; calculator results depend on the inputs you supply.

Start with the work on the page

The most useful introduction is something you can read or use. Start here offers a short route through the site, with clear distinctions between essays, practical guides, fictional examples, and outside resources.

For introductions and profiles, use the short biography. For a shared interest, a thoughtful disagreement, something you are making, or a simple hello, get in touch.
